t.4.60.2: O venerable one, because I am covered with wounds and my senses are disturbed by shame, I am utterly exhausted and cannot frame my words to speak.
t.4.60.1: Then I told the sage everything about that terrible, hard deed done out of rashness, and also about the following of the sun.
t.4.60.4: On the peak of Kailāsa, having made a wager in the presence of the sages, we resolved that the sun must be followed all the way to the great mountain Asta.
t.4.60.3: Jaṭāyu and I, two heroes deluded by pride, flew up into the sky out of rivalry, each eager to test his prowess.
t.4.60.5: Then we two, having arrived there together, looked down upon the surface of the earth and saw the cities, each one separate, appearing no larger than chariot wheels.
t.4.60.6: Somewhere we two heard the sounds of musical instruments and the sounds of Vedic chanting, and we two saw many women clad in red garments, singing.
t.4.60.7: Swiftly flying up into the sky and stationed on the path of the sun, we two look down upon that forest set amid green meadows.
t.4.60.8: The earth appears covered with mountains as though with pebbles, and the land is wrapped about by rivers as though by threads.
t.4.60.10: Then profuse sweat, exhaustion and fear came upon the two of us; bewilderment overcame us, and from that bewilderment a terrible swoon.
t.4.60.9: Himavān, Vindhya, and Meru, that very great mountain, shine upon the surface of the earth like elephants in a lake.
t.4.60.11: Neither Yama's southern quarter, nor Agni's south-eastern quarter, nor Varuṇa's western quarter could be made out; the world seemed held fast, struck down and burnt as if by fire at the end of a yuga.
t.4.60.12: With great effort we gazed once more at the sun, and the sun appeared to the two of us equal in size to the earth.
t.4.60.13: Then Jaṭāyu, without taking leave of me, fell down to the earth. Seeing him, I swiftly let myself drop from the sky.
t.4.60.15: I suspect that Jaṭāyuṣa fell down in Janasthāna, while I, my wings burnt, fell upon the Vindhya and was left benumbed.
t.4.60.14: Shielded by me with my two wings, Jaṭāyu was not burned, but through my own carelessness I was scorched there, falling from the path of the wind.
t.4.60.16: Bereft of my kingdom and of my brother, of my wings and of my prowess, wishing in every way only to die, I shall throw myself from the peak of the mountain.
